questions.question: What happens to a bone when an attached muscle contracts?
options: The muscle exerts a force on the bone, causing it to move.
The muscle pushes the bone away, causing it to lengthen.
The bone exerts a chemical force that dissolves the muscle.
The bone remains completely stationary and rigid.

questions.question: Which field of study focuses on the movement of bones and the forces exerted by muscles?
options: Biochemistry
Biomechanics
Bioengineering
Biotechnology

questions.question: What is the term for the turning effect of a force when a bone pivots around a joint?
options: Friction
Gravity
Pressure
A moment

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the moment when a bone pivots at a joint?
options: Its size cannot be determined because biological forces fluctuate too much.
Its size can be calculated based on force and distance.
It is always equal to zero regardless of the muscle force.
It is only present when a muscle is completely relaxed.

questions.question: What is the structural term used to describe the location where bones meet in the body?
options: Ligaments
Joints
Marrow cavities
Tendons

questions.question: How do skeletal muscles interact with the skeletal system?
options: They can move bones.
They absorb calcium from bones to stay healthy.
They act as cushions to prevent bones from touching.
They produce the bone marrow inside the bones.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes how muscles exert force to move bones?
options: They can only push, by relaxing.
They can both push and pull with equal strength.
They can only pull, by contracting.
They do not exert physical force but use chemical signals to slide bones.

questions.question: Because muscles can only pull, how do they typically work to move bones back and forth at a joint?
options: In antagonistic pairs, where one contracts while the other relaxes.
In identical pairs, where both contract at the exact same time.
By rotating around the bone in a spiral motion.
By converting into bone tissue temporarily.

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement about the composition of the human body?
options: It contains muscles.
It contains only bones and has no muscle tissue.
It is entirely made of bone marrow.
It lacks muscles but uses water pressure to move.

questions.question: What type of structure is a muscle in the human body?
options: A single large, non-living calcium structure.
A type of tissue made up of specialised cells.
An inorganic mineral deposit.
A liquid-filled sac with no cellular structure.

questions.question: Which two states are muscles capable of transitioning between to function?
options: Freezing and melting
Calcifying and dissolving
Contracting and relaxing
Expanding and evaporating

questions.question: What two key substances do muscles require from the body in order to contract?
options: Carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Sugar and oxygen
Calcium and carbon monoxide
Protein and hydrogen gas

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists different types of muscle found in human organ systems?
options: Cardiac muscle, smooth muscle and skeletal muscle
Rough muscle, soft muscle and hard muscle
Outer muscle, inner muscle and protective muscle
Brain muscle, lung muscle and bone muscle

questions.question: What is the structural framework of the human body, and what is it made of?
options: A skeleton made up of bones
A protective shell made of keratin
A network of fluid-filled cartilage tubes
A solid block of calcium carbonate

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct definition of a joint?
options: A type of blood vessel that carries oxygen to muscles.
Where two or more bones meet.
The outer layer of skin protecting a bone.
A bundle of nerve cells that controls movement.

questions.question: What are two main functions of the human skeleton?
options: Producing oxygen and storing excess sugar.
Supporting the body and providing protection for organs and tissues.
Contracting to move blood and digesting nutrients.
Controlling thoughts and regulating body temperature.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the nature of bones?
options: They are non-living structures made entirely of rock-like minerals.
They are made of living tissue made up of cells.
They are hollow tubes filled only with air.
They are flexible bands of muscle fibers.

questions.question: What vital component of the blood is produced inside the bone marrow?
options: Red and white blood cells
Blood plasma proteins only
Carbon dioxide molecules
Sugar and oxygen molecules
